summaries.demographer: An 18-year-old Chinese-American single female, native-born in Ellensburg, WA, currently living in her parents' owned home with both biological parents, a younger brother, paternal grandmother (6 months/year), and a dog (Q05, Q11, Q51, Q86, Q87). She just completed an Associate of Arts in Communications at Central Washington University and is awaiting a UW transfer decision (Q01, Q90, Q91). Household income is upper-middle-class (~$195K combined from RN mother and electrical-engineering father at BPA) with employer health coverage and no household debt risk (Q40, Q74, Q103, Q106). She is a never-married non-religious Democrat in her first electoral cycle (Q23, Q84, Q94, Q95).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Qiao exhibits low present financial pressure due to parental support, which lowers her risk aversion around career exploration and lets her favor a low-paid creative/communications track over a higher-earning nursing path (Q02, Q40, Q81). She makes spontaneous, identity-expressive purchases (used Sigma lens) but pays the credit card monthly and maintains a small Roth IRA at her father's prompting — signaling internalized long-horizon scaffolding from immigrant parents (Q56, Q61, Q63). Peer influence is high: friends (Maya, Priya, Linda) shifted her career choice, politics, and creative direction (Q02, Q24, Q65). Loss aversion is mild and primarily reputational/relational (fear of being a financial burden, anxiety about UW decision) rather than monetary (Q18, Q83).
summaries.political_scientist: Qiao is a high-engagement young Democrat with progressive Pacific Northwest values: climate, immigration, pro-choice, pro-union (Q23, Q24, Q95). Her institutional trust skews toward science institutions (CDC), local journalism (NPR), and certain progressive politicians (Jayapal) while being cautious of social-media medical info, indicating discriminating but not generalized trust (Q42, Q48). Civic participation is robust for her age: BLM march attendance in 2020, festival organizing, multicultural student-group volunteering, first-time voter (Q23, Q26, Q29, Q65). She holds a coalitional, multiracial framing of American identity and pushes her own family toward solidarity with Black communities, suggesting an emerging activist sensibility tempered by pragmatism on policing (Q26, Q27, Q28).
summaries.psychologist: Qiao presents as high in Openness and Extraversion, moderate Conscientiousness (forgets alarms, dishes-eventually, skips cool-downs), moderate-to-high Agreeableness, and moderate Neuroticism with subclinical anxiety (Q15, Q17, Q32, Q45). Her self-concept is bicultural and integrative — pride in Chinese heritage paired with PNW outdoorsy identity — which she uses adaptively for sense-making and career direction (Q01, Q108). Coping leans toward behavioral activation (hiking, photography, cooking, friend contact) over substance use or rumination, with mom and Maya as central attachment figures (Q38, Q43, Q44). Motivationally she is intrinsically driven by creativity, communal belonging, and meaning-making, with mild future-self anxiety about financial autonomy serving as a productive rather than paralyzing pressure (Q45, Q83, Q108).
